title: SRD coverage: swarms
summary: Independently authored GURPS builds for the 9 swarm identities issue #36 enumerates. A swarm is one multi-body creature, not a group, and the batch is built to say so: every record appears as exactly one — the builder refuses a swarm spec that claims otherwise — and every one buys Injury Tolerance (Diffuse), which is the trait that makes a sword useless against it. Damage is stated as literal dice rather than derived from ST, because a swarm's bite is a property of how many small bodies are in the hex and not of any one of them pushing; the builder takes literal dice only where a spec states them. Size Modifier is the space the swarm fills, not the size of any body in it. The attacks allow no roll and no active defence, which is the whole reason swarms are frightening and also the reason the rating path can see them at all.

monsters.name: Centipede Swarm
monsters.lair: The floor of a crypt or a rotten cellar, under everything that has not been moved in years.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: Everything in the swarm's hex is bitten, with no attack roll and no defence. Roll HT against the accumulated venom or lose the use of a limb to cramp and swelling.

monsters.description: The floor moves. A thousand hand-length centipedes pouring out from under a flagstone, going up boots and into sleeves, and each bite is nothing until you have taken forty of them. Stamping helps less than it should.
notes: One hex of swarm, which is where the Size Modifier comes from; no individual in it is larger than a finger.
Damage is stated as literal dice rather than derived from ST. A swarm has no meaningful Strength — the injury comes from how many mouths are in the hex.

monsters.name: Locust Swarm
monsters.lair: None. It arrives with the wind and leaves when there is nothing green left.

attacks.name: Storm of Bodies
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. The injury is trivial; the effect is that nobody in the hex can see, hear an order, or keep their mouth shut long enough to cast.

monsters.description: It is not really trying to hurt anyone. A locust swarm is a wall of insects that strips a season's crop in an afternoon and happens to be crossing the road, and the danger to a party is being inside it — blind, deafened, and unable to say anything without eating one.
notes: One hex, which is the game entity. A true plague is many of these across a horizon, and a GM wanting that should place several rather than enlarging one.
The threat is obscurement rather than injury, which is why the disabling ability carries more of the rating than the damage does.

monsters.name: Spider Swarm
monsters.lair: A web-choked corner of a ruin, with an egg sac above the doorway.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. Roll HT against the combined venom of several hundred bites or take fever and a shaking hand for the rest of the day.

monsters.description: An egg sac breaks and the ceiling comes down in pieces, and the pieces are moving. Individually harmless, in these numbers a spider swarm gets inside armour, inside sleeves, and inside the neck of a cloak, and there is nowhere to hit it that does any good.
notes: One hex of swarm, which is where the Size Modifier comes from.
Clinging matters here: this swarm arrives from above, and the ceiling is where it was waiting.

monsters.name: Swarm of Bats
monsters.lair: A cave roof or a belfry, and the column of them that leaves it at dusk.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. The bites are minor; the swarm's real effect is that anyone inside it is blinded, buffeted and unable to hold a line.

monsters.description: Hundreds of them coming out of a shaft at once, filling the passage wall to wall. Nothing in the swarm can hurt a person much on its own and none of that matters — you cannot see, you cannot hear an order, and the torch has already gone out.
notes: One hex of swarm; the individual bat is the Bat record in the bird-fish-aquatic batch.
Sonar is why a light does nothing to it. Darkness is not this creature's problem.

monsters.name: Swarm of Insects
monsters.lair: Standing water, a midden, or a corpse nobody found.

attacks.name: Bites and Stings
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. Roll HT or spend the fight swatting: any task needing concentration, and any spell, fails while the swarm is on you.

monsters.description: Whatever the region breeds — hornets, biting flies, ants boiling up out of the ground. It does not care about armour and it cannot be frightened off, and the party's spellcaster is going to have a much worse time than the party's fighter.
notes: One hex, and deliberately generic: the SRD heading covers whatever stings locally, and the mechanics are the same either way.

monsters.name: Swarm of Poisonous Snakes
monsters.lair: A den pit under a ruin, where they have wintered together for longer than the ruin has been empty.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. Roll HT at a penalty for the sheer number of doses; failure means the limb goes, then the breathing does. This is the most lethal thing in the batch and it is entirely chemical.

monsters.description: A den's worth of vipers, disturbed all at once and coming out over each other in every direction. There is no way through the hex that does not involve being bitten several times, and the venom does not care that each snake delivered only a little.
notes: One hex of swarm; the individual is the Viper Snake record in the snake batch.
The venom is priced at 40 points and carries most of the rating. That is correct — the bites themselves are trivial and the doses are what kill.

monsters.name: Swarm of Quippers
monsters.lair: A warm slow reach of river that everything local knows not to cross.

attacks.name: Feeding Frenzy
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. Everything in the water in that hex is being bitten continuously, and blood in the water makes it worse rather than better.

monsters.description: The water boils. A quipper shoal takes a pack mule down to bone between one bank and the other, and anyone still in the river when it arrives has about as long as it takes to shout. Getting out is the only tactic that works.
notes: One hex of swarm; the individual is the Quipper record in the bird-fish-aquatic batch.
This does the heaviest raw damage of any swarm here and has no disabling ability at all, which is the right shape: quippers do not disable, they consume.

monsters.name: Swarm of Rats
monsters.lair: A sewer, a granary, or the space between two walls.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. Every bite is filthy: roll HT afterwards or take a fever that arrives days later, when the party is somewhere less convenient.

monsters.description: The classic cellar encounter, and still a real one. A rat swarm goes over a person rather than around them, it does not break when hurt, and what actually costs a party is not the bites but what is in them a week later.
notes: Disease is priced as a disabling ability so the rating can see it. The bites alone would rate near nothing, which is not how a rat swarm plays out.

monsters.name: Swarm of Ravens
monsters.lair: A rookery in dead trees above a battlefield, a gallows, or a road with a bad reputation.

attacks.name: Beaks and Claws
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defence. Ravens go for the face and the eyes by preference: roll HT or fight blinded until the swarm is driven off.

monsters.description: Cleverer than anything else in this batch by a wide margin, and the only swarm here that seems to be choosing. A raven flock that has decided a party is worth mobbing goes for the eyes first, breaks off when it is losing, and comes back at dusk.
notes: IQ 5 is the highest in the batch and deliberate: corvids plan, and a GM should play this flock as though it has an opinion about who is dangerous.
